A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLoD-GS and retain matching methods and experiments. All pages, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering experiments, component ablations, and compression-transfer analyses, with quantitative results in Tables 1–9 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds FPS measurements, Mip-NeRF 360 evaluation, H-3DGS comparisons, and learned-parameter analyses.

M1.justification: The learned decay parameter, distance-dependent opacity, thresholding, virtual-distance sampling, and weighted regularization objective remain unchanged. Renaming the training strategy from coarse-to-fine to virtual distance scaling does not alter the documented procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual Mip-NeRF 360 evaluation in Appendix A/Table 4 and the FPS table. This extends real-scene coverage within the same static novel-view-synthesis task; BungeeNeRF, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending remain.

E2.justification: H-3DGS is added as an evaluated comparator on Tanks and Temples and Deep Blending in Tables 1–2. The existing 3DGS, Fast Rendering, Octree-GS, and MaskGaussian comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds FPS as an evaluation metric, speed-versus-quality/count measurements, and H-3DGS configurations with tau values 0, 3, 6, and 15. Existing splits, 30,000 training iterations, and activation after 5,000 iterations remain unchanged. The CLoD-GS scale settings already appear in v1.

E4.justification: Section 4.4/Figure 8 adds an Amsterdam case study examining how training scales affect opacity and learned decay-factor distributions. The existing component ablations, DLoD transition analyses, and transfer to MaskGaussian are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or performance uncertainty. The new parameter-distribution plots describe learned primitives rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial FPS, H-3DGS, and Mip-NeRF 360 results. Table 1 changes CLoD-GS BungeeNeRF LPIPS from 0.095 to 0.100 and Tanks and Temples SSIM/LPIPS from 0.853/0.170 to 0.843/0.185, matching the unchanged per-scene appendix values. Octree-GS primitive counts are replaced by missing entries. These are additions and reporting revisions, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the distance, masking, target-ratio, and loss definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Added parentheses around ReLU in Equation 2 only clarify notation; no new proofs or formal results appear.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces the comparative claim of state-of-the-art rendering quality with high rendering quality, narrowing the performance assertion. The central contributions of continuous LoD, a unified model, and reduced storage remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new decay-factor distributions as evidence that training learns greater primitive persistence. Appendix A acknowledges non-leading Mip-NeRF 360 quality, attributes it to shared hyperparameters without dataset-specific tuning, and presents this as a generality tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that hyperparameters are shared across datasets. Its reproducibility statement removes v1's assertion that model, training, and evaluation source code is included in supplementary material, without replacement access information. This establishes a disclosure change, not verified withdrawal of code.

R1.justification: v2 adds H-3DGS and Mip-NeRF 360 references and explicitly positions CLoD-GS as complementary to hierarchical systems through internal control of loaded chunks. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic details of retained works.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introduction and related-work passages, consistently renames the training strategy, revises headings, and adds an acknowledgement. Affiliation and publication-header text also change, while the overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 and adds the FPS and Mip-NeRF 360 tables plus runtime and parameter-distribution figures. Existing illustrations and appendix curves are retained, with relocation, resizing, shorter captions, and conference-style headers rather than wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: Direct FPS evidence in Table 2/Figure 4 strengthens the central efficiency argument, while additional comparisons and the acknowledged Mip-NeRF 360 weakness improve empirical coverage and claim calibration. Summary-table corrections also improve consistency with the retained appendix. These gains outweigh the reduced code-access disclosure, but incomplete timing details and the unchanged underlying validation limit the improvement.
